headline: Advance Daily Vehicle Permits for Superior Coastal Access
reservation: Ontario Parks utilizes a Daily Vehicle Permit system which may be required for guaranteed entry at specific high-traffic access points. Camping must be booked separately through the central Ontario Parks reservation portal. Availability often reaches capacity months in advance for the summer season.

days.title: Sacred Stones and Sandy Shores
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from Sault Ste. Marie

stops.name: Agawa Rock Pictographs
stops.detail: View ancient Indigenous rock paintings on a sheer cliff face, accessible only when Lake Superior's waters are calm.

stops.name: Agawa Bay
stops.detail: Walk the expansive cobble and sand beach to see the vast scale of the world's largest freshwater lake.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours to reach Agawa Bay; conditions vary on Highway 17.
days.note: Access to the pictographs is dependent on lake conditions; stay back from the ledge if waves are high.

days.title: Rugged Coastlines and River Gorges

stops.name: Sand River Falls
stops.detail: Follow the trail alongside a series of cascades that drop toward the Superior coastline.

stops.name: Katherine Cove
stops.detail: Explore the shallow, turquoise waters and rock outcrops that characterize this sheltered section of the park.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local movements; conditions vary.
days.note: Parking at Katherine Cove is limited and strictly enforced to protect the delicate coastal environment.

days.title: The High Cliffs of Old Woman Bay

stops.name: Old Woman Bay
stops.detail: Observe the 200-metre cliffs that resemble the profile of a woman's face in the rock formation.

stops.name: Nokomis Trail
stops.detail: Hike to the interior overlooks for a bird's-eye view of the bay and the surrounding boreal forest.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes from Wawa; conditions vary.
days.note: This northern end of the park can be significantly cooler and foggier than the southern Agawa section.

intel.title: Pictograph Access
intel.text: The lot for Agawa Rock is small and can fill by mid-morning during the summer peak. If full, proceed to the Visitor Centre and return later in the afternoon.

intel.title: Highway 17 Dead Zones
intel.text: Large stretches of the Trans-Canada Highway through the park have no cellular service. It is essential to have a physical map or downloaded GPS data for navigation and emergency reference.

intel.title: Last Service Points
intel.text: Fuel is not available within the park. Fill your tank in Sault Ste. Marie or Wawa before entering the park's 100km stretch of highway.

intel.title: Ice and Snow
intel.text: Late spring and early summer may still see ice on the lake or lingering snow on shaded trails. Verify trail conditions at the Agawa Bay Visitor Centre upon arrival.

intel.title: Seasonal Gates
intel.text: Park facilities and maintained roads are typically seasonal, operating from May to October. Highway 17 remains open year-round but can close during severe winter storms.

plan.arrival: Fly into YAM, pick up a rental vehicle, and stock up on all food and supplies in Sault Ste. Marie as options are limited near the park.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance vehicles are not required for the main highway, but those towing trailers should be aware of steep grades on Highway 17.
plan.goldenHour: Old Woman Bay is the premier location for viewing the sunset over the water, with the cliffs catching the light in late summer.
